heading: OmniNeural-4B Overview
content: OmniNeural is described by Nexa AI as the world's first NPU-aware multimodal model, designed specifically for Neural Processing Units. It natively understands text, images, and audio, and runs across PCs, mobile devices, automobiles, IoT, and robotics. A mobile phone NPU demo on the Samsung S25 Ultra is described as the first-ever fully local, multimodal, conversational AI assistant that hears you and sees what you see, running natively on Snapdragon NPU for long battery life and low latency. This model is referenced in both the AESOP Edge Model Guide (Razr Ultra only) and the Omni Claw NPU discussion. Per the user, it is already being superseded by whatever model they are currently running -- still considered cool, but not the long-term choice; some pieces of this README are worth carrying over into their own project's README.

heading: Key Features
content: Multimodal Intelligence processes text, image, and audio in a unified model for richer reasoning and perception. NPU-Optimized Architecture uses ReLU ops, sparse tensors, convolutional layers, and static graph execution for maximum throughput, claimed 20 percent faster than non-NPU-aware models. Hardware-Aware Attention tunes attention patterns for NPU, lowering compute and memory demand. Native Static Graph supports variable-length multimodal inputs with stable, predictable latency. Performance Gains are claimed at 9x faster audio processing and 3.5x faster image processing on NPUs compared to baseline encoders. Privacy-First Inference keeps all computation local: private, offline-capable, cost-efficient.

heading: Performance / Benchmarks
content: Human evaluation versus baselines: vision wins or ties in about 75 percent of prompts against Apple Foundation, Gemma-3n-E4B, and Qwen2.5-Omni-3B; audio shows a clear lead over baselines, claimed much better than Gemma3n and the Apple foundation model; text matches or outperforms leading multimodal baselines. Nexa Attention speedups: 9x faster audio encoding versus the Whisper encoder, 3.5x faster image encoding versus the SigLIP encoder. These are the vendor's own benchmark claims, not independently verified.

heading: Architecture Overview
content: OmniNeural's design is tightly coupled with NPU hardware: NPU-friendly ops with ReLU preferred over GELU/SiLU, sparse and small tensor multiplications for efficiency, convolutional layers favored over linear layers for better NPU parallelization, hardware-aware attention patterns to cut compute cost, and static graph execution for predictable latency.

heading: Production Use Cases
content: PC and Mobile: on-device AI agents combine voice, vision, and text, for example summarizing slides into an email on PC or extracting action items from chat on mobile; benefits are private, offline, battery-efficient operation. Automotive: in-car assistants handle voice control, cabin safety, and environment awareness, for example detecting an unbuckled child, a pet left in the car, loose objects, or road conditions like fog or construction; benefits are decisions running locally in milliseconds. IoT and Robotics: multimodal sensing for factories, AR/VR, drones, and robots, for example defect detection, technician overlays, mid-flight hazard spotting, and natural robot interaction; benefits include working without network connectivity.

heading: How to Use, Links, License
content: This is a mobile-only (Android) version; quickstart documentation is at docs.nexa.ai/nexa-sdk-android/quickstart. Links: Hugging Face at huggingface.co/NexaAI/OmniNeural-4B, site at nexa.ai, Discord at discord.com/invite/nexa-ai, X/Twitter at x.com/nexa_ai. Limitation: the current model is mainly optimized for English, with other languages planned as a next step. Citation: OmniNeural: World's First NPU-aware Multimodal Model, author Nexa AI, year 2025. License is Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial 4.0 (CC BY-NC 4.0) -- non-commercial use, modification, and redistribution permitted with attribution; commercial licensing contact is dev@nexa.ai. This confirms OmniNeural-4B is a real, currently-shipping Nexa AI product grounded in an actual SDK (pip install nexaai) and quickstart, not something AESOP or Omni Claw invented -- though given the user has since moved to a different model, this should be treated as historical/comparison reference rather than a locked-in dependency.
